what_happened: Research found the two territory-edge dependency tasks (430 feed_undeclared_implement_paths_into_file_scope, 446 close_the_plan_to_file_scope_reconciliation_gap) had already landed and were archived, and re-derived their actual landed shape from their own summaries rather than trusting the dispatch's forward-looking description. This directly determined the ruling: the general feedback mechanism mechanizes recovery but does not eliminate the follow-up-commit cost, so ruling (3) (subsumption) is not supported.

The dispatch's Option (2) (pre-commit requirement surfacing) targets a different failure mode than this record's LIVE SYMPTOM: an equivalent check (sync-manifest-scripts.sh --check / check-extension-docs.sh Rule Q, wired into verify-deploy.sh gate 3) already exists but runs post-redeploy, after the phase commit this record is about. The dispatch description did not mention this existing lint, which research surfaced via grep over check-extension-docs.sh and verify-deploy.sh.

Dispatch description cites git-commit-phase.sh's is_contained() at 'around lines 272-305'; re-derivation at plan time found it at lines 720-752 (normalization loop 730-732), with 272-305 now header prose about repository classification. Behavioural claim (trailing-slash defect closed) confirmed; only the line citation was stale.

The research report had already re-derived the three existing file_scope_arr splices, the sync-manifest-scripts.sh MATCHING rule, and the landed shapes of tasks 430/446/484, so plan decomposition needed only confirmation reads rather than fresh investigation.
